children: Five Narrow Lane, LP disclosed a 9.99% stake in Expion Energy, Inc.'s common stock. The filing, accepted on Aug. 28, 2026, follows an Aug. 21, 2026 private financing that included a convertible debenture and a warrant. The position is capped by a contractual 9.99% ownership limit despite additional conversion and warrant rights.

Five Narrow Lane invested through an 8% convertible debenture that will convert into Series A-1 preferred stock upon shareholder approval, along with a warrant for 1,058,609 common shares. The group also secured the right to buy up to $91 million of additional preferred stock and a right to participate in up to 33% of future equity sales. The filing notes a strict cap: “a contractually stipulated 9.99% ownership restriction.”

The investors say they bought the securities for investment and may talk with Expion Energy’s shareholders, executives, and directors about strategy. They may adjust their holdings over time, and until this filing date Joseph Hammer served on Expion Energy’s board. They highlight a key protection that lets them “participate in up to 33% of any subsequent issuance” on the same terms.

Five Narrow Lane, LP is a Delaware limited partnership with its principal office in New York. The fund receives services from LHX Corp., a family office where co-managing members Joseph Hammer and Arie Rabinowitz work. The partnership focuses on negotiated private placements and structured securities to build positions with governance and participation rights.
